pink primrose: A Primula species with soft pink, five-lobed flowers that bloom in low rosettes of crinkled leaves in early spring.
hard-leaved pocket orchid: A Paphiopedilum (slipper orchid) with a pouch-shaped lip and thick, leathery leaves, native to Southeast Asian forest floors.
canterbury bells: Campanula medium, a biennial with large, upright, bell-shaped flowers in blue, purple, pink, or white.
sweet pea: Lathyrus odoratus, a climbing annual with fragrant, ruffled flowers in shades of pink, purple, and white, popular in cottage gardens.
english marigold: Calendula officinalis, a bright orange-to-yellow daisy-like flower long used in traditional medicine and as an edible garnish.
tiger lily: Lilium lancifolium, with recurved orange petals covered in dark spots, and small bulbils forming in the leaf axils.
moon orchid: Phalaenopsis amabilis, a tropical epiphytic orchid with broad, flat, moth-shaped white flowers.
bird of paradise: Strelitzia reginae, whose orange and blue flowers emerge from a beak-like bract, resembling a crested tropical bird in flight.
monkshood: Aconitum, a tall perennial with hood-shaped purple flowers; every part of the plant is highly toxic if ingested.
globe thistle: Echinops, a spiky perennial with spherical, steel-blue flower heads that attract bees.
snapdragon: Antirrhinum majus, whose two-lipped flowers open and close like a mouth when gently squeezed, in a wide range of colors.
colt's foot: Tussilago farfara, a low perennial producing bright yellow, dandelion-like flowers on scaly stems before its leaves emerge.
king protea: Protea cynaroides, South Africa's national flower, with a huge artichoke-like flower head ringed by broad pink bracts.
spear thistle: Cirsium vulgare, a spiny biennial thistle with tufted purple flower heads atop winged, prickly stems.
yellow iris: Iris pseudacorus, a wetland perennial with bright yellow flowers and sword-shaped leaves, common along pond and stream margins.
globe-flower: Trollius, a buttercup relative with rounded, cup-shaped yellow flowers found in damp mountain meadows.
purple coneflower: Echinacea purpurea, a prairie perennial with drooping purple ray petals around a spiky orange-brown cone; used medicinally.
peruvian lily: Alstroemeria, bearing speckled, trumpet-shaped flowers in varied colors and prized as a long-lasting cut flower.
balloon flower: Platycodon grandiflorus, whose buds inflate like paper balloons before opening into star-shaped blue or white flowers.
giant white arum lily: Zantedeschia aethiopica, with a large, funnel-shaped white spathe wrapped around a slender yellow spadix.
fire lily: Cyrtanthus, a bulbous perennial bearing brilliant red-orange, flame-shaped tubular flowers.
pincushion flower: Scabiosa, a perennial with domed lavender-blue flower heads studded with protruding stamens, resembling a pincushion.
fritillary: Fritillaria, a bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped flowers, several species showing a distinctive checkered purple-and-white pattern.
red ginger: Alpinia purpurata, a tropical plant with waxy, bright red bracts that conceal its small true flowers.
grape hyacinth: Muscari, a small spring bulb producing dense spikes of tiny, round blue flowers resembling a cluster of grapes.
corn poppy: Papaver rhoeas, a wildflower with delicate, tissue-paper-like scarlet petals and a dark central blotch.
prince of wales feathers: Celosia argentea var. plumosa, with dense, feathery plumes of tiny flowers in vivid red, pink, or gold.
stemless gentian: Gentiana acaulis, a low alpine perennial with large, trumpet-shaped, intensely blue flowers held close to the ground.
artichoke: Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus, a thistle relative grown for its edible, unopened purple-flowered bud.
sweet william: Dianthus barbatus, a biennial pink relative bearing dense, flat-topped clusters of small, fragrant, bicolor flowers.
carnation: Dianthus caryophyllus, prized for its ruffled, clove-scented flowers in shades of pink, red, white, and yellow.
garden phlox: Phlox paniculata, a perennial bearing rounded clusters of fragrant, five-petaled flowers in pink, purple, or white.
love in the mist: Nigella damascena, whose pale blue flowers sit inside a delicate, thread-like ruff of feathery foliage.
mexican aster: Cosmos bipinnatus, an airy annual with daisy-like pink, white, or crimson flowers on tall, feathery stems.
alpine sea holly: Eryngium alpinum, a thistle-like perennial with spiny, metallic-blue bracts surrounding a cone of tiny blue flowers.
ruby-lipped cattleya: Cattleya labiata, a showy orchid with large lavender-pink petals and a ruffled, deep magenta lip.
cape flower: A common name for flowering bulbs native to South Africa's Cape region; in this dataset a star-shaped bloom with narrow, pointed petals.
great masterwort: Astrantia major, with a pincushion-like cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by a papery collar of star-shaped bracts.
siam tulip: Curcuma alismatifolia, a tropical ginger relative with upright pink or purple bracts resembling a tulip, though unrelated to true tulips.
lenten rose: Helleborus orientalis, an early-spring perennial with nodding, cup-shaped flowers in white, pink, or deep maroon.
barbeton daisy: Gerbera jamesonii, a South African daisy with large, brightly colored ray flowers in red, orange, pink, or yellow.
daffodil: Narcissus, a spring bulb with a central trumpet-shaped corona surrounded by six petal-like tepals, usually yellow or white.
sword lily: Gladiolus, with tall spikes of funnel-shaped flowers and stiff, sword-shaped leaves.
poinsettia: Euphorbia pulcherrima, whose showy 'petals' are actually red, white, or pink bracts surrounding small true flowers; a winter-holiday staple.
bolero deep blue: A rose cultivar bred for unusually deep, cool-toned lavender petals — true blue pigment does not occur naturally in roses.
wallflower: Erysimum, a fragrant perennial bearing clusters of four-petaled flowers in warm shades of orange, yellow, and maroon.
marigold: Tagetes, a compact annual with dense, ruffled orange or yellow flower heads and a pungent, distinctive scent.
buttercup: Ranunculus, a low perennial with glossy, cup-shaped yellow flowers common in meadows and lawns.
oxeye daisy: Leucanthemum vulgare, a wildflower with white ray petals around a flat yellow center, common in fields and roadsides.
common dandelion: Taraxacum officinale, a familiar lawn plant with a bright yellow composite flower head that matures into a spherical seed puff.
petunia: A garden annual with wide, trumpet-shaped flowers in a broad range of solid and patterned colors.
wild pansy: Viola tricolor, a small, low-growing flower with distinctive purple, yellow, and white 'face' markings on each bloom.
primula: Primula, a spring perennial forming rosettes of crinkled leaves topped by clusters of small, brightly colored flowers.
sunflower: Helianthus annuus, known for its large flower head of yellow ray petals around a dense brown disc, and for tracking the sun as a young plant.
pelargonium: Commonly called 'geranium' in gardens, a bushy perennial with rounded leaves and clusters of red, pink, or white five-petaled flowers.
bishop of llandaff: A dahlia cultivar with dark bronze-red foliage and single, brilliant scarlet flowers.
gaura: Oenothera lindheimeri, a wispy perennial with small, butterfly-shaped pink or white flowers that flutter on thin, wiry stems.
geranium: Hardy Geranium (cranesbill), a perennial with five-petaled purple, pink, or blue flowers and a distinctive beaked seed capsule.
orange dahlia: A dahlia cultivar with tightly layered, symmetrical orange petals radiating from a central disc.
pink-yellow dahlia?: A bicolor dahlia cultivar whose petals blend from pink at the tips to yellow near the center.
cautleya spicata: A ginger-family perennial with upright spikes of hooded yellow flowers emerging from maroon-tinged bracts.
japanese anemone: Anemone hupehensis, a late-summer perennial with simple, saucer-shaped pink or white flowers on tall, wiry stems.
black-eyed susan: Rudbeckia hirta, a cheerful wildflower with golden-yellow ray petals surrounding a dark brown, domed center.
silverbush: Convolvulus cneorum, a compact shrub with silvery, silky foliage and funnel-shaped white flowers with a yellow throat.
californian poppy: Eschscholzia californica, California's state flower, with silky, cup-shaped orange petals and finely divided blue-green foliage.
osteospermum: African daisy, with narrow, brightly colored ray petals — often purple, white, or pink — around a contrasting central disc.
spring crocus: Crocus vernus, one of the earliest spring bulbs, with cup-shaped purple, white, or yellow flowers emerging directly from the ground.
bearded iris: Iris germanica, distinguished by fuzzy 'beard' hairs on its lower petals and large, ruffled blooms in nearly every color.
windflower: Anemone, a woodland perennial with delicate, cup-shaped flowers that nod and tremble in the breeze.
tree poppy: Romneya coulteri, a shrubby perennial with large, crepe-paper white petals surrounding a dense boss of golden stamens.
gazania: A low, spreading daisy relative with brightly striped orange, yellow, or red petals that close in cloudy weather.
azalea: A deciduous or evergreen Rhododendron shrub covered in funnel-shaped flowers in vivid pinks, reds, purples, and whites each spring.
water lily: Nymphaea, an aquatic perennial with floating round leaves and star-shaped flowers that open on the water's surface.
rose: Rosa, the classic garden shrub prized for its layered, often fragrant petals and long history of cultivation and symbolism.
thorn apple: Datura stramonium, a nightshade with large, trumpet-shaped white flowers and spiny seed pods; all parts of the plant are toxic.
morning glory: Ipomoea, a fast-growing vine with funnel-shaped flowers that open at dawn and typically close by afternoon.
passion flower: Passiflora, a climbing vine with intricate, radially symmetric flowers featuring a distinctive fringed corona.
lotus: Nelumbo nucifera, a sacred aquatic plant with large pink or white flowers rising above the water on tall stems, symbolically significant across Asian cultures.
toad lily: Tricyrtis, a shade perennial with small, speckled, orchid-like flowers blooming in late summer and autumn.
anthurium: A tropical plant with a glossy, heart-shaped red or pink spathe surrounding a slender, spike-like spadix.
frangipani: Plumeria, a tropical tree with fragrant, five-petaled waxy flowers in white, yellow, and pink, commonly used in leis.
clematis: A climbing vine, often called the 'queen of climbers,' with large, star-shaped flowers in purple, white, pink, or blue.
hibiscus: A tropical shrub with large, trumpet-shaped flowers and a prominent, protruding central staminal column.
columbine: Aquilegia, a woodland perennial with distinctive spurred petals and nodding, bell-like flowers in bicolor combinations.
desert-rose: Adenium obesum, a succulent shrub with a swollen trunk and clusters of bright pink, trumpet-shaped flowers.
tree mallow: Lavatera, a fast-growing shrub bearing large, funnel-shaped pink flowers similar to hibiscus on tall woody stems.
magnolia: An ancient flowering tree genus with large, waxy, often fragrant blooms in white, pink, or purple that appear before or with the leaves.
cyclamen: A tuberous perennial with swept-back, butterfly-like pink or white petals above heart-shaped, often marbled leaves.
watercress: Nasturtium officinale, an aquatic edible plant with small, four-petaled white flowers, grown commercially as a peppery salad green.
canna lily: Canna, a tropical perennial with bold, paddle-shaped leaves and showy, ruffled flowers in red, orange, or yellow.
hippeastrum: Commonly called 'amaryllis,' a bulb producing a tall stem topped with several large, trumpet-shaped flowers.
bee balm: Monarda, a fragrant perennial with shaggy, tubular red or purple flower heads that attract bees and hummingbirds.
ball moss: Tillandsia recurvata, an epiphytic bromeliad forming grey-green tufts on tree branches and producing small, pale violet flowers.
foxglove: Digitalis purpurea, a tall biennial with a spike of tubular, spotted purple or white flowers; source of the heart medication digoxin.
bougainvillea: A woody vine whose true flowers are tiny and white, surrounded by large, vividly colored magenta, pink, or orange papery bracts.
camellia: An evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and rose-like, waxy flowers in white, pink, or red, prized in ornamental gardens.
mallow: Malva, a wildflower with five-petaled pink or purple flowers and a notched, crepe-textured bloom.
mexican petunia: Ruellia simplex, a fast-spreading perennial with funnel-shaped purple-blue flowers that open fresh each morning.
bromelia: A tropical bromeliad with a rosette of stiff leaves and a bold, spiky inflorescence in red, pink, or orange.
blanket flower: Gaillardia, a hardy wildflower with warm red-and-yellow banded ray petals around a domed center.
trumpet creeper: Campsis radicans, a vigorous vine bearing clusters of large, trumpet-shaped orange-red flowers attractive to hummingbirds.
blackberry lily: Iris domestica, with orange, red-speckled star-shaped flowers followed by seed pods that split to reveal blackberry-like clusters of black seeds.
